review_notes.tier_1_notes: Follow IPVV shape closely: real argument reconstruction with numbered steps, Sanskrit maxims quoted verbatim with [i.e.] unpacking, staged nanu/naca, numbered cruxes with scholar refs, Decision for L2 spine. Lore-primed with web scholarship. These are the gold standard.
review_notes.tier_2_notes: Follow IPVV shape but with varying depth. Bodhavilasa and Paryantapañcāśikā have good verse-by-verse reconstruction. Śivastotrāvalī is devotional prose — appropriate for the genre but less argumentative.
review_notes.tier_3_notes: Mechanical argmaps: template-generated with gloss + generic 'proceed as verse-by-verse' instructions. Need real argument reconstruction per verse. Kramastotra (30 files) and Stavacintāmaṇi (12 files) are the most mechanical. Bhairavastava, Bodhapañcadaśikā, Anuttarāṣṭikā, Bhairavānukaraṇa are smaller but also mechanical.
improvement_priority: Kramastotra: 30 verses, each needs real argument reconstruction. Most verses are single-line stotras; the 'argument' is the devotional stance. Priority: verses 1-5 (hymn's purpose), 10 (first means), 20 (six wheels), 24 (five acts), 28 (unobstructed self), 30 (seal).
Stavacintāmaṇi: 120 verses in 12 passages of 10. Each passage needs real argument reconstruction. Priority: p01 (supreme Lord), p04 (will and grace), p07 (devotion and grace), p12 (closing).
Bodhapañcadaśikā: 15 verses, each needs real argument reconstruction. Already has good C1.v2. Priority: p01 (one reality), p08 (limited light), p11 (non-knowledge), p14 (bondage/liberation).
Bhairavastava: 10 verses, each needs real argument reconstruction. Priority: p01 (veneration), p03 (suffering), p04 (fearlessness), p06 (bliss), p09 (obtaining).
Anuttarāṣṭikā: 8 verses, each needs real argument reconstruction. Priority: p01 (no method), p04 (bliss as forgotten treasure), p08 (all shines in consciousness-mirror).
Bhairavānukaraṇastotra: 5 passages, each needs real argument reconstruction. Priority: p01 (Consciousness-Bhairava as sole reality), p02 (weapons as liberating signs).

what_worked: Lore-prime (web search before mapping) significantly improved argmap quality — sambandhasiddhi and paramarthasara are the best examples.
Per-passage argmaps (md + json) follow IPVV shape and are machine-consumable.
L2.v2 (verse-by-verse plain English) with Sanskrit cited per verse preserves word pairings.
C1.v2 (final condensation) at 100-450w per passage is appropriately sized.
Registry (REGISTRY.json) tracks completion status and lore sources.
Skill (lore-prime-argmap) codifies the process for reuse.
what_needs_improvement: Mechanical argmaps (tier 3) need real argument reconstruction — the 'proceed as verse-by-verse' template is not useful.
L0 quality: some texts (sivastotravali, ajadapramatrsiddhi) have low PARSED rates due to format mismatch or long glosses.
L2.v2 for large texts (stavacintamani, kramastotra) is very long — the verse-by-verse format may need compression for readability.
C1.v2 for some texts is under 100w — the 100-450w spec is a guideline, not a hard rule, but consistency would help.
The 'post-session scholar sharpen' step should be more systematic — currently it's ad hoc web searches.
Need to verify L2.v2 against L0 (the ipvv spec requires every L2 sentence to link to L0).
next_steps: Improve tier 3 argmaps with real argument reconstruction (priority: kramastotra, stavacintamani).
Run verify.sh equivalent checks on translation-work texts.
Cross-reference L2.v2 with L0 records for traceability.
Consider compressing very long L2.v2 files for readability.
Add more scholar sources for tier 3 texts.
